climate_pressure: Dry conditions during the 2023–2024 El Niño cycle.
documented_impact: Conditions more favorable for clearing forest in the Colombian Amazon.
fcv_mediator: Existing dissident factions regulate and profit from land transactions, deforestation and cattle economies, amid shifting negotiations and state control.
possible_consequence: Armed actors can exploit dry conditions for revenue and bargaining leverage, as described by the study; no quantified increase in violence is established.
alternative_explanations: Political negotiations, group fragmentation, commodity incentives, land speculation and enforcement changes also influence behavior.
uncertainty: Qualitative subregional study using El Niño as a proxy; not attribution of the event to anthropogenic warming or causal identification of armed-group behavior.
resilience_factors: Community water conservation and restoration offer coping channels but need resources and safe institutional access.
compact_statement: The Guaviare study describes existing dissidents exploiting El Niño dryness for deforestation revenue and negotiating leverage, not climate causing an insurgency.

climate_pressure: Drought and environmental degradation in the Guaviare case-study area.
documented_impact: Communities require water conservation, restoration and environmental response.
fcv_mediator: Armed-group territorial control and insecurity limit state access and environmental operations.
possible_consequence: Environmental enforcement and reforestation responses are constrained, weakening support for longer-term resilience.
alternative_explanations: Agency budgets, technical capacity, weak state presence and resource shortages also limit response.
uncertainty: Subregional participant accounts, not a national estimate of conflict blocking all adaptation or a measured resilience effect.
resilience_factors: Community wells, Indigenous medicinal gardens and local restoration are documented coping efforts; outcomes were not evaluated.
compact_statement: Insecurity and territorial control restrict environmental response and reforestation in the Guaviare study area, not all Colombian adaptation.
